rules.title: Linked user requests
rules.description: User requests can be linked because they contain a unique identifier across sessions or services.
rules.mitigation: Use scoped, rotating pseudonyms or session-specific tokens instead of global identifiers.

rules.title: Linkable user requests
rules.description: User requests contain attributes that can be combined into quasi-identifiers (e.g. fingerprints, locations).
rules.mitigation: Minimize metadata transmission, generalize timestamps, and restrict client fingerprinting attributes.

rules.title: Linking through distinguishable patterns
rules.description: Patterns in request metadata, timing, or payload structure allow linking distinct requests to one user.
rules.mitigation: Introduce message padding, batch requests, or randomize dispatch intervals.

rules.title: Linkable dataset
rules.description: Stored personal or activity data contains fine-grained attributes that enable cross-record correlation.
rules.mitigation: Apply k-anonymity, differential privacy, or aggregate historical entries.

rules.title: Profiling users
rules.description: Analyzing data points for behavioral or emotional patterns to link actions and construct profiles.
rules.mitigation: Enforce explicit consent for profiling, provide opt-outs, and decouple analytical profiles from raw IDs.

rules.title: Identified user requests
rules.description: Incoming user requests contain explicit identity data (e.g. full name, email, credentials).
rules.mitigation: Avoid requesting direct identity data when pseudonymous authentication or zero-knowledge proofs suffice.

rules.title: Identifiable user requests
rules.description: Requests do not carry names but contain behavior or contextual attributes sufficiently unique to infer identity.
rules.mitigation: Generalize input parameters, coarsen location coordinates, and redact granular search parameters.

rules.title: Identifiable data flows
rules.description: Free-form or unconstrained user data (e.g. feedback, crash traces) contains accidentally submitted identifiers.
rules.mitigation: Implement automated regex or NER filtering to scrub personal attributes before payload ingestion.

rules.title: Identifiers in data requests
rules.description: Communication reuses universal identifiers across distinct third-party API queries or outbound calls.
rules.mitigation: Generate independent, transient tokens tailored strictly per external integration endpoint.

rules.title: Identifiable dataset
rules.description: Stored records contain combined demographic, operational, or location attributes that allow re-identification.
rules.mitigation: Apply l-diversity, t-closeness, or noise injection to stored analytical tables.

rules.title: Non-repudiation of service usage
rules.description: Users cannot deny having accessed a service because access logs tie session operations to explicit identities.
rules.mitigation: Segregate audit identities, use blind tokens, or purge non-essential access logs periodically.

rules.title: Non-repudiation of sending
rules.description: Transmitted payloads or messages are digitally signed, preventing data subjects from refuting authorship.
rules.mitigation: Use ephemeral keys or deniable authentication schemes if persistent non-repudiation is not legally required.

rules.title: Non-repudiation of receipt
rules.description: Outbound deliveries automatically trigger receipts, telemetry pings, or read markers confirming delivery.
rules.mitigation: Make delivery confirmations opt-in and eliminate automated tracking pixels.

rules.title: Non-repudiation of storage
rules.description: Data is stored on immutable or append-only structures, eliminating plausible deniability and right-to-erasure.
rules.mitigation: Store cryptographic commitments or off-chain state instead of persisting raw records on immutable ledgers.

rules.title: Non-repudiation of hidden data or metadata
rules.description: Document generation or image exports retain embedded author metadata, revision logs, or invisible watermarks.
rules.mitigation: Sanitize and strip EXIF, author tags, and build environment variables prior to document dispatch.

rules.title: Detectable users
rules.description: System responses differentiate between 'wrong password' and 'user does not exist', leaking identity status.
rules.mitigation: Return uniform generic error responses and equalize execution time for authentication failures.

rules.title: Detectable service usage
rules.description: Unencrypted or observable transmission endpoints allow network observers to detect interaction with the service.
rules.mitigation: Enforce strict TLS encryption, DNS-over-HTTPS, and mask server endpoint semantics.

rules.title: Detectable events
rules.description: Application events produce observable side effects (e.g. disk size shifts, bursts of traffic, temporary lock files).
rules.mitigation: Pad network packet lengths, normalize file processing sizes, and suppress public status indicators.

rules.title: Detectable records
rules.description: Data retrieval queries or error codes leak whether an individual record or identifier exists in storage.
rules.mitigation: Return standard HTTP 404 or generic access denial regardless of whether the record exists.

rules.title: Excessively sensitive data collected
rules.description: The application ingests finer-grained or more sensitive personal data than necessary for core features.
rules.mitigation: Remove ingestion of non-essential attributes (e.g. precise GPS, biometric vectors) at the boundary.

rules.title: Excessive amount of data collected
rules.description: System queries or collects records at higher frequencies or larger volume batches than strictly needed.
rules.mitigation: Throttle ingestion, batch summary rollups, and pull updates on demand rather than continuous streaming.

rules.title: Unnecessary data analysis
rules.description: Internal processes perform enrichment, automated classification, or analytics unrelated to primary service scope.
rules.mitigation: Decouple analytics pipelines and require operational isolation for post-processing routines.

rules.title: Unnecessary data retention
rules.description: Data is persisted indefinitely without time-to-live expiration or scheduled pruning procedures.
rules.mitigation: Implement automated cron jobs or database retention TTLs to delete stale records.

rules.title: Overexposure of personal data
rules.description: Personal records are shared broadly with external APIs, analytics partners, or client dashboards.
rules.mitigation: Apply strict output projections, whitelist exposed attributes, and audit third-party data flows.

rules.title: Insufficient transparency
rules.description: Data subjects submit information without clear disclosure of processing scopes, sinks, or downstream sharing.
rules.mitigation: Provide contextual, concise privacy notices at input collection forms.

rules.title: Insufficient information when sharing data of others
rules.description: Users upload address books, media, or third-party details without verifying consent or notice mechanisms.
rules.mitigation: Prompt uploaders for verification and provide opt-out channels for named third parties.

rules.title: Insufficient privacy controls
rules.description: The system does not offer user-facing controls to configure processing preferences, tracking toggles, or consent states.
rules.mitigation: Build preference management dashboards defaulting to highest-privacy configurations.

rules.title: Insufficient access
rules.description: Data subjects cannot retrieve, view, or export the personal records collected and stored about them.
rules.mitigation: Expose self-service data export APIs or standardized take-out archives.

rules.title: Insufficient rectification or erasure
rules.description: System lacks functionality allowing individuals to update inaccurate data or execute hard deletions.
rules.mitigation: Implement endpoints supporting atomic profile updates and hard record deletion cascading across stores.

rules.title: Non-compliance of processing with applicable regulations
rules.description: Personal data operations lack a documented legal ground (e.g. consent, contract necessity, legitimate interest).
rules.mitigation: Enforce legal basis tagging on all ingestion pipelines and block processing without valid basis flags.

rules.title: Non-adherence to privacy standards
rules.description: Architecture lacks documented adherence to established privacy engineering frameworks (ISO 27701, NIST Privacy).
rules.mitigation: Align telemetry, storage, and processing controls with NIST Privacy Framework or ISO/IEC 27701.

rules.title: Improper data lifecycle management
rules.description: Absence of structured lifecycle state transitions (collection, validation, archiving, permanent destruction).
rules.mitigation: Formulate programmatic data lifecycle state machines enforcing archival and deletion triggers.

rules.title: Insufficient security of processing
rules.description: Security measures fail to protect personal records against unauthorized processing, theft, or compromise.
rules.mitigation: Implement end-to-end encryption, strict role-based access control, and regular vulnerability scanning.
